title.narrative: Lean season malnutrition/GBV response provision of RUSF/Tom Brown for treatment of MAM. 0-59 Months in Mafa Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtBorno State is grappling with a severe humanitarian crisis, intensified by a complex interplay of factors, including protracted conflict, extreme weather events such as droughts and floods, economic instability, social unrest, and systemic governance failures. The cumulative impact of these challenges has led to widespread displacement, exacerbating poverty and vulnerability among the affected populations. Furthermore, Nigeria's economic woes have been compounded by alarming inflation rates, with food prices soaring to 40.9% and overall inflation reaching 34.2% as of June 2024, further straining the lives of already beleaguered citizens. Nigeria's economic struggles worsen as the Naira continues its downward spiral against the US dollar, with recent exchange rates hovering around N1,583.73/$1 at the official market and N1617/$1 at the parallel market. This depreciation, coupled with the devastating impact of climate change-induced floods in October 2024, which submerged roughly 1.6 million hectares of farmland, has led to staggering losses. The floods resulted in annual losses of approximately 1.1 million tons of essential crops like maize, sorghum, and rice, translating to nearly $1 billion in losses. The African Development Bank forecasts further depreciation, projecting a 6% decline in the Naira's value by 2025 due to global market volatility. Repeated shocks and crises have eroded livelihoods and diminished the capacity of the most vulnerable to cope. Bama has the 4th largest population of internally displaced persons (IDPs), reaching approximately 47,071 households (158,922 people), and the 6th largest local government area hosting returnees, with 14,111 families (58,743 people). Poor living conditions (44%) and military operations (20%) continue to trigger new arrivals from hard-to-reach locations. Persistent violence across the entire Northeast hinders food availability and access. Borno State has the highest number of food-insecure individuals (facing CH3 or worse conditions) and is at risk of sliding into catastrophic levels of food insecurity during the lean season. Nigeria faces a significant malnutrition crisis, with approximately 5.4 million children requiring urgent preventive and curative services. Bama is classified as IPC-AMN Phase 3 (Serious), and the looming lean season is expected to exacerbate the situation, potentially pushing vulnerable children into Phase 4 levels of malnutrition due to severe food insecurity. Efforts to restore livelihoods and provide durable solutions, including the relocation of internally displaced persons (IDPs) by the state government, are severely underfunded. According to the IOM-led intentions survey (April 2024), most IDPs are reluctant to relocate, citing concerns over hunger, inadequate nutrition, unemployment, poor housing conditions, and limited economic opportunities. Many IDPs face limited options, with durable solutions restricted to either returning to their place of origin or relocating to a new location, further complicating their situation.ltbrgtThe 2025 standard allocation will go a long way for SHI in supporting to reduce the impact of malnutrition as well as reduce the burden of GBV needs across mafa, Borno state, thereby significantly reducing the child mortality rate and protection cases. ltbrgtlt/pgt
